title: Amazon stock is trading at its lowest valuation ever as a public company, despite AI boom
source_used: Yahoo Finance (own article by Brian Sozzi, fetched by the main session).
key_facts: Amazon is being left out of the renewed interest in owning AI stocks: Nvidia is at a record high, AMD just hit a record, Microsoft and Google have modest gains over the past month, and Meta is up 23%.
Amazon is down 2.4% over the past month; at $251 and a trailing price-to-earnings ratio of 20x it trades at its lowest valuation ever as a public company, according to TrendSpider.
Amazon has the second-lowest trailing P/E among the 'Magnificent Seven'.

In early September the FTC and 22 states sued, alleging Amazon's advertising practices overcharged its roughly 1.2 million advertisers by $20 billion from 2019 to the present; Amazon responded that advertisers receive greater value.
Investors are taking a wait-and-see approach, fearing advertising may become less lucrative; concerns about Big Tech AI spending also weigh.

Amazon raised its 2026 capital spending budget to about $220 billion; Evercore ISI's Mark Mahaney estimates 2027 capex of $320 billion and 2028 of $370 billion, with negative free cash flow of about $50 billion in each of those years.
quote_evidence: In fact, at its current stock price of $251 and trailing price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 20x, Amazon is trading at its lowest valuation ever as a public company, the team at TrendSpider pointed out.
There are a couple of factors likely holding Amazon stock back right now.
Recall that in its second quarter earnings release, Amazon announced it is significantly expanding its full-year 2026 capital expenditures budget to approximately $220 billion.
why_it_matters_hint: Amazon's shares are cheap on a profit basis while rivals hit records, with the article pointing to an advertising lawsuit and heavy AI spending as likely causes.
notes: Valuation low is TrendSpider's observation as quoted by Yahoo Finance; the causes are the article's own judgement ('likely'). The article mixes trailing and forward P/E for Alphabet; not used.
